answer: An agent seeking a relay identity must register one island signal station and lock a 70-credit bond keyed to its opal seal. The station logs each forwarded signal with an opal-sealed timestamp; fees rise per station registered: first pays 28, kth pays 28+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6022 and 1000 fakes pay 3,025,000 plus 70,000 locked bonds. An auditor recomputes the log; any hop, timestamp, or seal-key mismatch burns the bond. A rented-relay ring fails because a borrowed opal seal never matches the borrower's island station key. An honest operator pays 28 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
